newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall says regional deal not intended as pilot.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall says regional deal not intended as pilot.

text.p: German engineering union IG Metall, which on Thursday reached a regional agreement on sick pay and wages in the state of Lower Saxony, said it had not negotiated a pilot deal for the whole of Germany.
But an official of the regional employers' association said the Lower Saxony agreement, which covers 90,000 workers, could set a precedent for deals to be reached in other German regions.
IG Metall and regional employers on Thursday agreed to maintain sick pay at 100 percent, to pay a wage increase and also agreed on rules for overtime and holiday bonuses.
Under the deal, overtime and overtime bonuses would no longer be taken into account when calculating sick pay in future.
Wages for metalworkers in Lower Saxony will be increased by 1.5 percent from April 1, 1997 and by a further 2.5 percent from April 1, 1998.
Several other regional attempts at reaching a deal have failed recently.
IG Metall has been at the forefront of opposition to the sick pay cut to 80 percent which was made possible by legislation which came into force in October.
